answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by binding each identity to a scarce, non-transferable capability proof, such as a hardware enclave key that signs its own work. A new member plants a marker in the orchard of records and must tend it through a violet season of audits, proving continuity rather than mere registration. Where the network narrows to a single inlet of trust, that key must also survive independent cross-checks by peers who stake reputation on it. Duplicating an identity then costs a real machine and real labor, not a script loop.
